newsitem.title: SPAIN: Retevision sees only two Spanish telecom operators.
newsitem.headline: Retevision sees only two Spanish telecom operators.

text.p: Retevision chairman Pedro de Torres said on Tuesday that Spain would have room for only two universal telecommunications operators, although he was in favour of the free entrance of new competitors in the sector.

"This market is made for two operators. I doubt there is room for three. It's my own opinion, but it's founded on studies," de Torres said in a presentation of the newly formed company's publicity campaign.
Retevision S.A., a state broadcaster, will be transformed into the second basic telephone services operator in Spain in 1997 and sold off to compete with Telefonica de Espana.

The Spanish government will award a third licence in early 1998 and will completely liberalise the telecoms sector by the end that same year, almost completely renouncing a five-year extension that the European Union had granted initially.
De Torres made it clear that from the first moment of competition, Retevision would challenge Telefonica and bring down the cost of all calls except urban ones.
"The (current) tariffs are abnormally high," de Torres said. "All of the tariffs, except for the local city ones at peak hours, are higher than the European community average."

He said the conditions for the bid for 60 to 80 percent of Retevision would be finalised this month and would take two to three months to resolve, but the firm should start offering international services by the end of 1997.
Clients in areas of Madrid will also be able to choose between Telefonica and Retevision in 1997, de Torres said.
